l0.question: Conditional on a real PIT-observable operating transition, does an independently observable recognition/consensus gap identify which transitions are economically selectable (not-yet-recognized) versus already-recognized?

chain.definition: Business transition actually occurring and PIT-observable independently of recognition.
Latest lawful contemporaneous consensus/expectation state known at decision_as_of.
Reality has moved farther than contemporaneous recognition; exact operator deferred to L2.
Later recognition state; included in the causal story but not opened as D7 timing research.
Later D6 selection enrichment under a separately preregistered wager law; not evaluated here.

l1.h1: Among firms exhibiting a real operating transition, future economic selection enrichment under a later preregistered wager law is higher when contemporaneous consensus recognition materially lags the observed transition, versus transitions already recognized.

family_boundary.tr_v0_estimand: Reality + RecognitionGap versus Reality alone conditional on Reality already being present.

recognition_contract_pre_l2.pit_law: available_at <= decision_as_of; latest lawful vintage only; source receipt bound; observed consensus and inferred market-implied state remain explicitly distinct.

falsifiers.F1: Recognition cannot be defined independently of future returns -> KILL.
falsifiers.F2: Recognition is merely another encoding of the same transition -> KILL / not incremental.
falsifiers.F3: Hypothesis materially identical to CRV1 -> MERGE/ROUTE.
falsifiers.F4: Useful recognition state only after inspecting failed FTK dates/payoffs -> KILL.
falsifiers.F5: Mechanism requires choosing H/K/threshold from prior economic residuals -> KILL.
